The '''2020–21 season''' was [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]]'s 29th season in the [[Premier League]] and 43rd successive season in the top division of the [[English football league system]]. After finishing sixth in the [[2019–20 Premier League|2019–20 league season]], Tottenham entered the [[2020–21 UEFA Europa League|UEFA Europa League]] at the second qualifying round, ultimately reaching the round of 16 in the competition where they were eliminated by [[GNK Dinamo Zagreb|Dinamo Zagreb]]. In the [[2020–21 FA Cup|FA Cup]], the club was knocked out by [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] in the fifth round.

In the [[2020–21 Premier League|Premier League]], Tottenham lost their first game at home to Everton, but then went on an unbeaten run into December, topping the league standings for four weeks. With an away loss to [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], the team's form dropped. [[José Mourinho]] had guided the club to the [[2020–21 EFL Cup|Carabao Cup]] [[2021 EFL Cup final|final]], where they would face [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]]. However, because of the dropped form in the league, he was sacked along with his coaching staff on 19 April 2021,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2021/april/club-statement/|title=Club statement|access-date=19 April 2021|date=19 April 2021|work=Tottenham Hotspur F.C.}}</ref> and replaced by former player [[Ryan Mason]] as interim head coach until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2021/april/coaching-update/|title=Coaching update|access-date=21 April 2021|date=20 April 2021|work=Tottenham Hotspur F.C.}}</ref> Mason's first game in charge was against [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] at home, which Tottenham won. The next game was the Carabao Cup final, where Manchester City narrowly prevailed 1–0.

This season was notable for [[Gareth Bale]]'s return from [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] on loan for a season-long second stint at Tottenham, the first time he played in North London after [[2012–13 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season|2012–13]].

===FA Cup===
{{main|2020–21 FA Cup}}

===EFL Cup===
{{main|2020–21 EFL Cup}}

The draw for both the second and third round were confirmed on 6 September, live on [[Sky Sports]] by [[Phil Babb]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Carabao Cup: Round Two and Three draw confirmed |url=https://www.efl.com/news/2020/september/carabao-cup-round-two-draw-confirmed/ |access-date=6 September 2020 |work=English Football League |date=6 September 2020}}</ref> On 21 September, Tottenham's third-round game against [[Leyton Orient F.C.|Leyton Orient]] was postponed due to multiple [[COVID-19]] positive tests among the Leyton squad.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54237123 |title=Leyton Orient confirm 'number of players' have coronavirus |work=BBC Sport |date=21 September 2020 |access-date=23 September 2020 }}</ref> On 25 September, the [[English Football League]] issued a statement saying that it "has determined that in line with Carabao Cup Rule 5.1, the Club <nowiki>[Leyton Orient]</nowiki> was unable to fulfil its obligations to complete the fixture by virtue of the Council’s order and shall therefore forfeit the tie" and that "in accordance with Carabao Cup Rules, Tottenham Hotspur have been awarded with a bye to progress to Round Four of the Carabao Cup",<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2020/september/efl-update-leyton-orient-v-tottenham-hotspur/ |title=EFL update: Leyton Orient v Tottenham Hotspur |work=Tottenham Hotspur F.C. |date=25 September 2020 |access-date=18 October 2020}}</ref> where they played [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]. The game finished 1–1, and went straight to a penalty shoot-out which Tottenham won 5–4 to progress into the next round. Tottenham won their quarter-final against [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] by a 3–1 scoreline to advance to the semi-finals. In the semi-finals, played over only one leg, Tottenham then beat 10-man [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]] 2–0 to progress to the [[2021 EFL Cup Final|final]] of the competition, which they lost 1–0 against [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]].

=====Round of 32=====
The draw for the round of 32 was held on 14 December 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0263-10f42a348589-e77f1a9ee84d-1000--last-32-draw-lowdown/|title=Europa League round of 32 draw: all you need to know|date=1 December 2020|website=[[UEFA]]}}</ref>

=====Round of 16=====
The draw for the round of 16 was held on 26 February 2021.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0266-11a3825ca928-faf7a4d65919-1000--draw-all-you-need-to-know/|title=Europa League round of 16 draw: all you need to know|date=26 February 2021|website=[[UEFA]]}}</ref> The order of legs was reversed after the original draw to avoid a scheduling conflict with the [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] v [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]] second leg in the same city on 18 March, as Arsenal were the domestic cup winners and given higher priority over Tottenham.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0267-11b187e265ef-db799ea6eb72-1000--tottenham-dinamo-legs-reversed/|title=Legs reversed for Tottenham-Dinamo Zagreb UEFA Europa League round of 16 tie|website=[[UEFA]]|date=1 March 2021|access-date=1 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11675/12232854/europa-league-tottenhams-last-16-games-with-dinamo-zagreb-reversed|title=Europa League: Tottenham's last-16 games with Dinamo Zagreb reversed|publisher=Sky Sports|date=1 March 2021|access-date=1 March 2021}}</ref>
